full_caption: Cinderfield Development Partners, L.P., Appellant, v. Horatio Jarrowmere, Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Cinderfield Development Partners, L.P. and Horatio Jarrowmere own riparian tracts along the Kestrel River within Pinecrest County. The dispute concerns Horatio Jarrowmere's diversion of approximately 950 gallons per minute for irrigation of 5.2 acres.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: A prescriptive water right may be acquired by open, adverse diversion for the statutory period, but only as against a use that was actually interfered with during that period.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: The public trust doctrine reserves to the State title to the beds of navigable waters. Navigability for title purposes is determined by susceptibility to commercial navigation at the date of statehood.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: A use that wholly deprives a downstream riparian of water for domestic purposes is unreasonable as a matter of law, without regard to the economic value of the upstream use.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Groundwater in this State is governed by the rule of reasonable use, under which an overlying owner may withdraw for beneficial use on the overlying land but may not export off-tract to the injury of neighboring wells.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: Accretion belongs to the riparian owner; avulsion does not change the boundary. The 1999 channel shift, being sudden and perceptible, was avulsive and left the boundary at the former thread of the stream.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: The accommodation doctrine required Horatio Jarrowmere to consider directional drilling from an off-site pad before siting the wellpad within the irrigated circle. Failure even to evaluate the alternative defeats the claim of reasonable necessity.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: The injunction is modified to permit diversion not exceeding 100 gallons per minute between May and August, and is otherwise affirmed.

sections.heading: RIDER D — SEVERED MINERAL ESTATE AND SURFACE ACCOMMODATION
sections.text: The owner of the severed mineral estate may use so much of the surface as is reasonably necessary for exploration and production, and shall accommodate existing surface uses where a reasonable alternative means of extraction exists. Before siting any wellpad within an irrigated area, the operator shall evaluate in writing off-site and directional alternatives and shall furnish that evaluation to the surface owner not less than 60 days before entry.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Notice
sections.text: Every notice required or permitted shall be in writing and shall be deemed given: on personal delivery; on the third business day after deposit in the United States mail, certified, return receipt requested, postage prepaid; or on the next business day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier. Notices to a party shall be sent to the address last furnished by that party in writing. Electronic mail alone does not constitute notice unless the recipient acknowledges receipt in writing.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Time of the Essence
sections.text: Time is of the essence as to every obligation stated in this instrument. Where the final day for performance falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday in the State of Brightwater, the period is extended to the next business day.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Counterparts and Electronic Signature
sections.text: This instrument may be executed in counterparts, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one instrument. A signature delivered electronically has the same effect as an original, provided that any instrument submitted for recording shall bear original signatures and acknowledgment before a notary public of the State of Brightwater.

sections.heading: Clause 4 — Governing Law
sections.text: This instrument shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Brightwater, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles. Any action arising out of or relating to this instrument shall be brought exclusively in the courts sitting in Pinecrest County, Brightwater, and each party consents to the personal jurisdiction of those courts.
